finding: No test lists a fold-matching name that is a different file, so the same-file check in _stored_name is unpinned
why: Mutants `os.path.samefile(path, path)` and `if _fold(name) == fold or os.path.samefile(...)` at publish_bug_mode.py:592 pass all 88 tests, yet on this machine's NTFS (case-blind, normalization-sensitive) they return a different file's spelling, which changes the work id D-35 says must stay one per file.
fix: Add a case whose listing holds a fold-matching decoy that is a different file (e.g. listed ('e\u0301.md', '\u00e9.md'), typed '\u00c9.md', samefile true only for '\u00e9.md') and assert the result is '\u00e9.md'.
evidence: test line 1018: `monkeypatch.setattr(mode.os.path, "samefile", lambda a, b: True)  # every entry is one file`; the only other samefile stubs are name-lowercase equality (line 981) and always-False (line 990). Full-suite mutation run: `samefile-self SURVIVED | 88 passed`, `fold-return-no-samefile SURVIVED | 88 passed`. Real NTFS probe: dir holds 'e\u0301.md' (other file) and '\u00e9.md' (typed file), typed '\u00c9.md': original returns '\xe9.md', both mutants return 'e\u0301.md'.
